problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=⟨\sqrt{4-t},\,{t}^{2}-1,\,(t-2)^{3}⟩.$
worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\sqrt{4-t}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,4].$

- The domain of the 2nd component ${t}^{2}-1$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $(t-2)^{3}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14033854/assets/af217bfbda3db04572cbfbb0b1aa8c18a6bb94c127c3d034dbfe3d96d6abbf80.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in (-\infty ,4].$
